evidence: The paper employs random forests and XGBoost as components of an ensemble forecasting model: "The ensemble model was constructed as a combination of three different statistical forecasting approaches: exponential smoothing [35], random forests [36] and XGBoost models [37]." However, the paper contains no reporting, discussion, or interpretation of variable importance from these models. Random forests are used purely for predictive forecasting of antimicrobial resistance rates; all reported conclusions focus on cost-effectiveness metrics and predicted AMR trajectories, not on feature importance rankings or magnitudes.
